clue.text: See 14
Element put away, little one

parts.note: neon is a chemical element, a noble gas
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: Someone tidies away a chemical sample and mentions a small child in the same breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn baby, which is certainly a little one.

clue.text: Plant belonging to you and me

parts.note: thy is the old possessive form of you
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener says a particular plant is shared property between the two of you.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a herb grown in gardens, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Published remarkable children's author

parts.note: a newspaper ran a story when it published it
some, as in 'that was some party', means remarkable

explanation.surface: A tribute to a writer for young readers who got into print and was outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons and other novels for young readers.

clue.text: Small curl cut back

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a crimp is a wave or curl put in hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser trims a little curl short.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise, reducing spending stingily.

clue.text: See 14
See 19
Slice passed round if a terribly cold dessert

indicators.note: the slice is wrapped around the other letters, as if passed round them

parts.note: a slice is a part or portion

indicators.note: terribly suggests the two little words are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A portion of something gets handed round if it is very cold, like an ice-cream treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed' could look like a second piece of wordplay, but 'passed round' together is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parfait is a frozen or chilled layered sweet made with cream, served as a pudding.

clue.text: Indication of sorrow as holiday cancelled — blast!

parts.note: a tear shows that someone is sad
taken as written
a trip is a short holiday
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: Someone weeps because their holiday has been scrapped, and curses.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast someone, or tear a strip off them, is to reprimand them severely.

clue.text: See 27
Injuring knee lower, dagger's first to go in — is that sharp practice?

indicators.note: to go in means this letter is placed inside the rearranged ones
injuring suggests the words knee and lower are damaged and twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of dagger's is used

parts.note: its opening letter is D

explanation.surface: A violent scene: a knife wound below the knee, and the question whether that counts as dirty dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injuring' rearranges KNEE LOWER, and 'to go in' places D from 'dagger's first' among those letters. Sharp practice usually means dishonest dealing; here it is practice with sharp needles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing and embroidery involve constant use of pointed needles, so they are literally practice with sharp things.

clue.text: Look behind outhouse initially for shelter in garden

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of behind and outhouse are taken

parts.note: first letter B
first letter O

explanation.surface: Someone glances behind the garden shed for somewhere to shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small roofed open structure in a garden, giving shade or cover.

clue.text: Spooner's trailing man in protective clothing

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of the words are swapped, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a man is a guy; the AT of 'at rear', the sense of trailing, is said along with it, giving GUY AT
something trailing is at the rear; its AT goes with the man, leaving rear

explanation.surface: A reference to the Reverend's man following along behind, dressed for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: Trailing means at the rear, so the phrase said aloud is GUY AT REAR; Spooner swaps the opening G and R sounds to give RYE-AT GEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Riot gear is the helmets, shields and padding police wear to protect themselves at disturbances.

clue.text: Where virtual reality experienced, not liking New York art museum?

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
averse means disinclined or opposed

explanation.surface: A question whether disliking a famous gallery is where you go to get a simulated experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first; the parts come in the reverse order to the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The metaverse is an online space of immersive simulated worlds that people enter through headsets.

clue.text: Go and howl back?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to go is a euphemism for using the lavatory
second meaning, playful: a wolf howling in reply to the wild is responding to the summons of the wild world

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a plain verb of movement; here it is the polite euphemism for relieving oneself. The second reading takes the phrase literally, with nature calling and an animal replying.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a euphemism for urinating or defecating, and read literally it describes responding to a cry from the wild.

clue.text: See 25
Really, really, unexceptional

parts.note: so, as in 'it is so cold', means really
a second so for the second really

explanation.surface: A shrug of a review: very, very ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so-so is mediocre, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Thick-soled shoe, it's said to shock in burlesque

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a burlesque is a comic parody, a skit
boo is the word shouted to startle someone

explanation.surface: A clumpy shoe in a comic stage show is reportedly meant to startle the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski boot is chunky footwear with a rigid sole that clips into skis.

clue.text: Stick and stone grow

parts.note: a prop is a stick or pole used as a support
agate is a semi-precious stone

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: a stake and a rock help things grow.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate plants is to breed or multiply them, making them grow.

clue.text: Ancient city, show one that is knocked over

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial show or display

indicators.note: knocked over in a down clue means these letters are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A tour of an ancient site in which one exhibit gets toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'knocked over' turns the two pieces upside down, which reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was a Roman town buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Where leader seemingly subservient, lightweight agent said 'go to work'

indicators.note: to work means these letters are put to work, reworked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A minor spy was told to get to work, in a situation where the boss seems to be bossed.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'go to work' disguise the fact that 'go' is fodder and 'to work' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a situation where a minor part controls the whole, so the one nominally in charge is really following.

clue.text: Always at the top, superior team evidently rested excellent offensive player

indicators.note: in a down clue each word's top is its first letter, and always means every word in the run

parts.note: first letter S
first letter T
first letter E
first letter R
first letter E
first letter O

explanation.surface: A sports report: a dominant side clearly rested its star attacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' looks like part of the football picture, but it is the definition: a record or music player.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a sound system that plays music, so it is a player of records or CDs.

clue.text: Turning over place, one wicked party!

indicators.note: turning over means the letters of the three pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to put something is to place it
I is the Roman numeral for one
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: Someone trashing a place and calling it one wicked party.
explanation.definitionFit: To live it up is to celebrate and enjoy oneself lavishly, as at a party.

clue.text: One ridiculing another drink served by barista, audibly?

indicators.note: audibly means the word is heard, a sound-alike of the drink

parts.note: a mocha is a coffee with chocolate, made by a barista

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at another person's order in a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the drink and the word for a scoffer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocker is a person who scoffs at or derides someone else.

clue.text: Rake, for example, up bum

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a cad

indicators.note: up in a down clue means these letters are read from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A garden rake shoved up someone's backside, an absurd bit of slapstick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like a noun for a backside but is the verb, as in to bum a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum something is informal for scrounging it, which is what cadging means.

clue.text: Runner accepts cost for getting treatment — what needs paying?

indicators.note: accepts means the river takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: the Dee is a river, and a river runs, so crosswords call it a runner

indicators.note: getting treatment means the words cost and for are worked on and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An athlete pays out for physiotherapy and asks what the bill is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it is the river Dee, which flows through Chester and Aberdeen; 'getting treatment' works on COST FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical consultation charge is a bill the patient owes after being seen.

clue.text: Dali appears surreal in skilful training exercise

indicators.note: in means the reworked name sits inside the other word

parts.note: deft means skilful

indicators.note: surreal, Dali's own art movement, suggests his name is distorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The painter Dali turns up looking dreamlike in a clever gym routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlift is a weightlifting move in which a barbell is raised from the floor to hip height.

clue.text: See 19
Bit of a thinker devising a ploy in bed

indicators.note: devising suggests the letters are worked into something new, a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thinks up a scheme while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bed' reads as a location for the scheming, but all of 'a ploy in bed' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineal body is a small gland in the brain, so it is part of anyone who thinks.
